sections.h2: Where is the Putnam County recorder in Ottawa?
sections.html:
The Putnam County Recorder works from 245 E. Main Street in Ottawa, the same street address the county auditor lists. The recorder's resources page gives a phone of 419.523.6490, a toll-free line at 888.638.0042 and a fax at 419.523.4403.

The office opens at 8:30 and closes at 4:30 on weekdays, while the recording window shuts at 4:15. The contact page also lists the days the office closes: New Year's Day, Martin Luther King Day, Presidents Day, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day, Labor Day, Columbus Day, Veterans Day, Thanksgiving and Christmas.

Ottawa is the county seat. Wikipedia notes an 1820 creation date, an 1834 organization date, and a name honoring Israel Putnam. The Blanchard River, an early travel route for settlers, crosses the county.

sections.h2: In what sequence does a Putnam County deed get recorded?
sections.html:
Three stops come before the recorder sees a deed, and the county auditor's page spells them out. The order matters, because an unstamped deed is turned away.

  1. Take the legal description to the Tax Map Office, which sits in the engineer's office and answers at 419-523-6931. All legal descriptions must be pre-approved, and the document must meet the county's conveyance standards.
  2. Once the tax map staff sign the document, bring it to the auditor, who transfers it and collects the conveyance fee.
  3. Record the transferred deed with the recorder, who follows the standards and fees on its own site.

The auditor is at 245 East Main Street in Ottawa, 419-523-6686, on a weekday 8:30 to 4:30 schedule. Under Tools on its site sits a calculator that prices the transfer before you go.

sections.h2: What does the Putnam County auditor charge to transfer a deed?
sections.html:
On its transfers page the auditor lists four dollars for each thousand of price, with the price rounded up to the next hundred, and fifty cents a parcel in transfer fee. The conveyance is not processed unless the check matches the conveyance fee to the penny.

Form DTE 100 accompanies a normal sale, and DTE 100 (EX) is the version for deeds that claim an exemption. The county's forms page carries both, so you can fill them in ahead of the visit.

A separate county transfer tax is possible under R.C. 322.02, capped at 30 cents on each $100 and owed by the grantor. Whether Putnam has one in force is a question for the auditor; the calculator gives the quickest total.

sections.h2: How much does recording cost in Putnam County?
sections.html:
The recorder's FAQ points to a fee page and says the office charges a $4.00 fee for each marginal notation. The base amounts come from the statute, R.C. 317.32.

  • Pages one and two: $34 together, half base fee and half housing trust fund.
  • Later pages: $8 each, split the same way.
  • A preservation surcharge, capped at $5 an instrument, goes to the county's general fund.
  • A certified copy costs $2 a page in total.

A document that fails the county's standards costs $20 more. Those rules, under R.C. 317.114, call for 10-point type or larger, dark blue or black ink, no highlighter, and letter or legal paper. Page one needs three inches clear at the top, later pages an inch and a half, and the sides and bottom an inch. Exempt are court papers, plats, DD 214 discharges, state and federal documents, and anything signed before July 1, 2009.

sections.h2: Which Putnam County offices matter in a home sale?
sections.html:
The table sets out what each office prints for the public, drawn from the county's own sites.

AuditorTransfers the deed, collects the conveyance feeFour dollars per $1,000 and 50 cents a parcel; 419-523-6686

The auditor's home page also posts a delinquent real estate list and counts 29,689 parcels as of 2023. Sellers with a house that may have fallen behind should check that list.

sections.h2: How can I record a Putnam County deed electronically or by mail?
sections.html:
The recorder's e-recording page says the service now covers deeds and other transfer documents, and names three approved vendors: Simplifile at 1.800.460.5657, CSC at 1.866.652.0111 and Erecording Partners at 1.888.325.3365. You work through one of them rather than the county directly.

The FAQ describes how fast things move. Documents recorded at the counter go back immediately, documents e-recorded are returned immediately, and documents delivered by mail are sent out the next business day. The office also requires a full legal description, including on releases and assignments, and maintains tract indexing by geography.

Paying at the counter is simple: the FAQ says checks are made payable to the Putnam County Recorder. The same page says releases and assignments need a full legal description too, so a mortgage satisfaction cannot be recorded on a bare parcel number. If you are mailing a paper, allow for the next-business-day return and for the time the auditor's transfer takes first.

Records search is online. The FAQ says the indexes are open to everyone, viewing images needs a free online subscriber form, and documents are indexed on the computer starting January 1, 1993. A recording notification service is also offered.

sections.h2: What tools does the Putnam County auditor's site offer sellers?
sections.html:
Its Tools menu holds sales reports, delinquency reports, the conveyance calculator and a tax estimator. A GIS parcel viewer sits behind the Map link, and an Info section holds the forms the state and the office provide.

The same page posts the 2025 delinquent parcels list. Search your parcel before listing, and phone the auditor if the record looks off.

sections.h2: What else does the Putnam County recorder do?
sections.html:
Beyond deeds, the office runs the county's Ohio Century Farm registrations. A farm qualifies after 100 years in one family, and the recorder will meet with a family to check eligibility. It also keeps military discharge records, which are the DD 214 files veterans need for benefits.

Putnam County is mostly rural. Wikipedia's 2020 figures: 34,451 people over 484 square miles, with 84.2% living in rural areas and owners occupying 83.8% of occupied homes. The county board of education operates nine school districts.

Long-held land is a point of pride here. A farm owned by one family for 100 years can be registered, and qualified registrants receive an heirloom certificate signed by the Governor and the Director of the Ohio Department of Agriculture. A yard sign is available for purchase. The recorder will meet with you to check eligibility, so ask before you sell a farm that might qualify.

Wikipedia counts 12,976 households and 13,824 housing units in the county, 6.1% of them vacant.

A farm, an estate home or a house with a balance owed still goes through the same paperwork, and a cash buyer can purchase it in present condition and cover these fees at the closing table.

faqs.q: What are the Putnam County recorder's hours?
faqs.a: Doors are open weekdays from 8:30 to 4:30, with recording accepted from 8:30 to 4:15. The office closes on the holidays its contact page lists.

faqs.q: What does the Putnam County auditor charge for a deed transfer?
faqs.a: Four dollars per thousand of price, rounded up to the next hundred, plus fifty cents a parcel. The check has to equal the conveyance fee exactly.

faqs.q: Do I need approval before I bring a deed to the Putnam County recorder?
faqs.a: Yes. The Tax Map Office in the engineer's office must clear the legal description, and the auditor must transfer the deed before it reaches the recorder.

faqs.q: Does Putnam County accept e-recorded deeds?
faqs.a: Yes. E-recording now covers deeds and transfer documents, through the vendors the recorder lists: Simplifile, CSC and Erecording Partners.

faqs.q: How much is a marginal notation in Putnam County?
faqs.a: $4.00 for each one, per the recorder's FAQ. A nonconforming document costs $20.00 more.
